chunks: ʿUmar ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever buys an animal should stand on its left side, take its forelock with his right hand, and recite over its head Sūrat al-Fātiḥah.
And the two Muʿawwidhatayn, and the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the end of Banī Isrāʾīl.
“Say: Call upon Allāh or call upon al-Raḥmān.”
And Āyat al-Kursī, for that is protection for that animal from afflictions.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Throne Verse, recited here as a source of protection.
key_terms.أَمَانُ: Protection or safety granted against harm.
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two sūrahs of seeking refuge, namely al-Falaq and al-Nās.
key_terms.دَابَّةً: A riding or domesticated animal being purchased.
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, recited here for blessing and protection.
key_terms.نَاصِيَتَهَا: Its forelock, which the buyer is instructed to hold.

ai.seo_question: What should be recited in Shia hadith when purchasing an animal for protection from afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a recommended supplication and recitation to be performed when purchasing an animal. It combines specific bodily etiquette with recitation of Qur'anic passages as a means of seeking divine protection from harm and affliction.
